title: Chopin, Nocturne Op. 9 No. 2: Lévy and Prati
work: Nocturne in E♭ major, Op. 9 No. 2
question: Lévy and Prati play the melody as its ornaments grow more elaborate at each return.
intro: Frank Lévy and Patrizia Prati play the piece. It begins with a leap from B♭ to G over the left hand’s rocking bass and chords. Each time the melody returns it carries more ornaments, and a short cadenza follows.

recordings.label: Frank Lévy, c. 2014
recordings.note: A pupil of Maria Tipo and Leon Fleisher, Lévy made this recording for Musopen’s Chopin project.

recordings.label: Patrizia Prati, 2015
recordings.note: Prati recorded twelve Chopin nocturnes at Madrid’s Museum of Romanticism on 24 November 2015.

passages.label: Melody and accompaniment
passages.note: The melody lies above the left hand’s recurring bass note and the two chords that follow it.

passages.label: Cadence in E♭
passages.note: A leap into the treble is followed by a falling run; the phrase returns to E♭.

passages.label: Trill on a held note
passages.note: A trill is played on a held note before the melody continues its descent. The left hand keeps the same rocking pattern.

passages.label: Ornamented return of the melody
passages.note: The tune returns with small, quick notes wound around its longer ones. The bass repeats its earlier pattern.

passages.label: Melody in paired notes
passages.note: The right-hand melody is played in paired notes, then short, detached chords lead to its next return.

passages.label: Rise in octaves before cadenza
passages.note: The right hand climbs into octaves and the music grows louder shortly before the cadenza.

passages.label: E♭ chords after the cadenza
passages.note: After the cadenza, quiet arpeggiated E♭ major chords bring back the pulse and lead to the soft close.
